Subject: Tiered Recovery SLA & Planned Outage Runbook — redline packet

Sara,

Attached is the redline packet for the MSA + Order Form focused on SLA and planned outage sequencing. Highlights for your review (top-level):

- Tiered recovery commitment: propose 99.95% monthly uptime for PROD (multi-region) and 99.0% for non-prod.
- P1 response: 15 minutes (24/7), P2: 1 hour (business hours), P3: 24 hours.
- Service credit caps: sliding scale tied to monthly invoice (see section 3 of the PDF).
- Planned outages: recommend two maintenance windows per month, 02:00–04:00 PT (non-business hours) with automatic prefix caching to reduce client impact. For any outage >2h or cross-region failover we ask for 48-hour notice and a runbook share.

We included an operational runbook stub (Planned_Outage_Runbook_v1.docx) that outlines rollback steps, communication cadence, and postmortem deliverables. Laura is looped in on legal redlines.

Next steps: please review the PDF and runbook and flag any items you want in a marked-up counterproposal. If there are firm constraints from procurement/legal on credit caps or notice periods, point those out and we can propose alternatives (e.g., fallback model variant or temporary burst credits).

Thanks,

Chloe Martin

Chloe —

Thanks for the packet. I reviewed with our legal and infrastructure teams; attached is a short counterproposal (Orion_Counterproposal_SLA.docx) with the primary asks summarized here:

1) Uptime target: Orion can’t accept 99.95% as a default for single-region PROD. We need 99.9% guaranteed or multi-region wording that makes redundancy explicit.
2) Service credit cap: propose a hard cap of 5% of monthly fees per month for all credits combined.
3) Response windows: P1 response of 30 minutes during our business hours (7am–7pm PT) is acceptable; outside business hours we expect an on-call acknowledgment within 60 minutes.
4) Maintenance notice: any maintenance >1 hour should have 30 days’ notice if it impacts core inference endpoints. Shorter unplanned maintenance must be limited to emergency patches only.
5) Audit/evidence: please provide SOC 2 Type II report and a short security runbook for changes that touch customer data.

We want to keep this moving—procurement will need to see a redline addressing caps and notice windows before routing to our CFO.

Best,

Sara Jones
Sr. Counsel, OrionData
Sara.Jones@oriondata.com

Attachment: Orion_Counterproposal_SLA.docx

Sara — thank you for the detailed feedback. Quick replies inline below and attached an updated redline (Redwood_SLA_Redline_v2_marked.pdf) that incorporates the concessions we can agree to.

- Uptime target: we can rework the language to make 99.95% contingent on multi-region active/passive deployment and customer enablement of cross-region failover. If Orion opts not to enable cross-region we’ll default to 99.9% for single-region PROD.
- Service credit cap: we can move to a 10% monthly cap, but we’ll provide a one-time mitigator — a credits escrow and a credit-first remediation plan for first occurrence in a 12-month period.
- Response windows: we can accept your business-hours compromise for P1 (30 min) but we will maintain a 15-minute P1 SLA for customers on Dedicated plans. For hosted customers like Orion we’ll honor 30 minutes during 7am–7pm PT and 60 minutes outside that window.
- Maintenance notice: we can accept 30-day notice for planned maintenance impacting core inference endpoints >2 hours. For the regularly scheduled maintenance windows (our proposed two per month 02:00–04:00 PT), we’ll give 7 days’ advanced notice and maintain a published maintenance calendar. Emergency patches remain excluded and will be limited to safety/security fixes with postmortem.
- Audit pack: Laura will coordinate delivery of SOC 2 Type II and a brief security change runbook.

Action items:
- Laura: legal to produce single-sheet concession language and an appendix that can be inserted into the order form.
- Marissa: sales to confirm procurement timeline and whether a PO will be issued instead of DocuSign.
- Hannah: ops to attach an abridged runbook and confirm rollback ETA expectations for >2h events.

Sara, can procurement confirm which of the two levers (credit cap at 10% + escrow vs credit cap 5% fixed) is a hard blocker vs negotiable? If escrow is unacceptable, we’ll tee up the 5% fixed cap option for commercial review.

Thanks — I’ve attached the marked-up PDF and an updated runbook with clearer rollback steps.
